consequences: The specification fixes size = octets following the size field; the published example byte 0x40 is treated as a documentation defect and is not copied into vectors.

Vector book-composite encodes the size as 0x3F, and vector book-composite-published-size asserts that the published byte 0x40 is rejected as a decode error, so the disagreement is tested in both directions rather than silently smoothed over.
A recorded third-party capture of an equivalent composite exchange would settle this from practice; until then the reading rests on the array example, which is exact.
evidence: The array example (picture.9/picture.19) is arithmetically exact under this reading: 0x25 = 37 = count octet (1) + element constructor (1) + elements (15 + 20). Under the other reading it would be 35, and the depicted second element carries no constructor of its own.

Under the same reading the compound worked example is inconsistent with itself: its list8 size byte reads 0x40 (64) where the depicted content is count (1) + title (23) + authors array (38) + null isbn (1) = 63 = 0x3F. Every other length byte in that example is exact (0x11 = 17 for "example:book:list", 0x15 = 21, 0x0E = 14, 0x13 = 19), and 0x40 is a round value, so the size byte is most likely illustrative rather than computed.

The layout figure (picture.8) labels the region after the count field as "count items", which is consistent with the size covering the count field, though its alignment does not settle the question on its own.
question: For compound encodings (list8/list32, map8/map32), does the size field count the octets that follow it (count field plus items), and does the array size field likewise count its count field?

readings.name: Follows the size field
readings.statement: size = count field + items (arrays: count + element constructor + elements), excluding the size field itself.

readings.name: Items only
readings.statement: size = items only, excluding both the count field and the size field.
